proposal: The Mandate recommends placing political appointees in State leadership from the first day (including non-Senate-confirmed posts), increasing the number of political appointees, accepting the resignations of all political ambassadors, and quickly reviewing all career ambassadors, with immediate recall of those in countries where policy will change substantially or who have shown hostility to the administration. It sets no fixed share among political, Foreign Service and civil service ambassadors and says ambassadors with personal ties to the President should go to key posts such as the UK, Japan, Australia, the UN and NATO.

status_summary: On 2025-01-20 State asked senior career officials in leadership posts, including the acting Under Secretary for Political Affairs and other under and assistant secretaries, to leave those posts; they stayed in the Foreign Service. In December 2025 the administration told career chiefs of mission or senior embassy officials in at least 29 countries that their tenures would end in January 2026; State called this a standard process and said ambassadors are the President's personal representatives, chosen to advance his agenda. As of July 2026, AFSA data reported by Ballotpedia showed 107 of 195 ambassador posts vacant and 91.1% of second-term ambassador appointments going to political appointees; the Senate confirmed 11 ambassadors in a 74-nominee single vote on 2026-08-07 (Reuters).

timeline.event: Senior career diplomats serving in State's top leadership posts were told on Inauguration Day to resign or leave those posts; the group included the acting Under Secretary for Political Affairs and the other under and assistant secretaries. They were not fired and remained Foreign Service officers. (Article date approximated to the event date.)

Senate Republicans used the procedure known as the nuclear option to change confirmation procedure for Trump nominees (headline-level evidence; article body not read). Batch votes covering ambassadors followed, as in the 2026-08-07 vote below.

AP reported that chiefs of mission in at least 29 countries (13 in Africa) were told their tenures would end in January 2026. State called it routine for an administration and said ambassadors represent the President personally. The diplomats can take other assignments and remain in the Foreign Service.

Ballotpedia, citing AFSA data, reported 107 of 195 ambassador posts vacant (54.9%), with 34 nominees pending and 73 posts lacking a nominee, and a second-term appointment mix of 8.9% career and 91.1% political (prior-administration averages cited: 31.9% political since Ford, 43.5% in Trump's first term, 40.8% under Biden).
The Senate confirmed 74 nominations in one 51-47 vote, including 11 ambassadors and 5 ambassador-rank nominees, a fraction of the more than 100 vacancies (Reuters).
The Senate confirms nominations en bloc under S.Res.817 by 51 to 47 (roll call vote 225); press reports say the package included 11 ambassadors, a count not shown on the roll call page.

The Democratic ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee says only 13 career ambassadors have been confirmed in this administration and over 100 diplomatic posts remain empty, and asks for unanimous consent to confirm 10 career nominees (partisan statement).

title: Reset the ambassador corps and State leadership with new political appointees
uncertainties: No primary government document was found for the January 2025 departures or the December 2025 recalls: State declined to confirm names, and the AP report relies on unnamed officials. One primary source exists for the confirmation step: Senate roll call vote 225 (second session, 119th Congress) records the 2026-08-07 en bloc confirmation under S.Res.817 at 51 to 47. That page lists no ambassador count, so the Reuters figure of 11 ambassadors among 74 nominations is unverified here, and the congress.gov text of S.Res.817 could not be opened (robots restriction). The AFSA tracker page was read only through a summarizing fetch, and its counts are approximate. A Democratic ranking member's release of 2026-10-01 says only 13 career ambassadors have been confirmed, over 100 posts are empty and more than 30 career ambassadors were recalled; this is a partisan statement and differs slightly from AP's count of at least 29 countries. Whether ambassadors were told to resign before 2025-01-20 (the Mandate asked for this) was not verified. The search cap ended before State statements could be searched.
